analysis_notes.gap_analysis: The Torah text (torah_75.txt) contains no explicit בְּחִינַת equating language. The teaching draws an a-fortiori (קל וחומר) argument: if Torah's inner light returns a person to the good, then certainly the light of the tzaddik (whose gazing alone helps for holiness) is even greater. This is a causal/eitza structure throughout. The five concepts that appear in the text — הסתכלות בצדיק (gazing at the tzaddik), תלמיד חכם (the Torah scholar), תורה (Torah), אור הצדיק (the tzaddik's light), and קדושה (holiness) — are not equated to each other via bechina; they form a causal chain. The dataset correctly captured only the eitza edge הסתכלות בצדיק → קדושה. No bechina additions are warranted.
